market.headline: Premarket pop fades: SPY slips red and QQQ drops 1% as chips slide again, but TSLA clings to a gain into opex
market.note: The hot import prices and strong factory data gave SPY an early lift, but it faded minutes after the open and SPY is now slightly red. QQQ is down about 1% with INTC, MRVL and META leading watchlist losses, so leadership is still thin. TSLA cut its 3% premarket gap to about 1% after tagging 363.37. On an opex Friday, watch whether SPY gets pinned near Thursday's 771.79 close into the final hour.

portfolio.note: Green today because the TSLA stack (TSLA, TSLL, TSLW) is up while QLD lags with QQQ. The week is still deep red from the TSLA slide since last Friday.

watchlist.note: Premarket pop faded, now just under Thursday close
Down about 1% as chips and META weigh
3% premarket gap cut to about 1%, low so far 363.37
Holding up better than the rest of the chips
Lower into earnings Wed Oct 21 after the close
2x Nasdaq, so the QQQ drop hits double
Worst mover on the list early
One of the few greens on the list

catalyst.outlook: Inflation is still the story, and the open shows the market knows it. September import prices rose 1.1% and are up 8.1% year over year, the hottest annual pace since mid-2022, while industrial production jumped 0.7%. Growth is fine, but with CPI at 3.7% and PPI hot, rate-cut hopes stay on a short leash into the Oct 27-28 Fed meeting, and that hits long-duration tech first, which is why QQQ is lagging SPY. Posts on X are flagging how narrow this tape is, with the index near highs while a big chunk of stocks sit well off theirs. A real turn needs chips to stop sliding. Next week for you is Wednesday night: TSLA and META both report.

today.name: Import Prices (Sep)
today.read: Hotter than expected and August was revised down to 0.5%. Fuel imports rose 4.8% and nonfuel 0.7%. Year over year import prices are up 8.1%, the largest gain since July 2022. That keeps pressure on yields and growth names like TSLA and QQQ even as the index holds near highs.

today.name: Industrial Production (Sep)
today.read: A clear beat. Manufacturing rose 0.3%, utilities jumped 3.5%, and third-quarter IP ran at a 2.8% annual rate. Growth is holding up despite hot energy costs, which softens the stagflation read from this week's inflation prints.

today.name: Capacity Utilization (Sep)
today.read: Utilization moved up but remains 2.5 points below its long-run average, so factory tightness is not the main inflation driver. Still a mild hawkish tilt alongside hot import prices.

today.name: Monthly options expiration
today.read: Big SPY and QQQ option positions roll off today, which can pin prices near large strikes and cause sharp moves in the last hour.

week.name: Cboe extended options hours begin
week.why: Early morning and late sessions start for SPY, QQQ and more. Expect thinner liquidity and wider spreads in those windows.

week.name: NAHB Housing Market Index (Oct)
week.why: Builder mood with mortgage rates above 7%. A read on how rates are biting the housing side of the economy.

week.name: Housing Starts and Building Permits (Sep)
week.why: More housing data. Weak numbers would support the case for easier policy despite hot inflation.

week.name: Netflix earnings (after the close)
week.why: First mega-cap tech report of the season. Sets the tone for growth names into TSLA and META.

week.name: TSLA, META, IBM, LRCX, TXN earnings (after the close)
week.why: The big one for you. TSLA margins, robotaxi and Roadster plans, plus META AI spend and LRCX and TXN reads on the chip slump.

week.name: Initial Jobless Claims
week.why: Claims have hovered near 200K. A jump would be the first crack in the labor market.

week.name: S&P Global Flash PMIs (Oct)
week.why: First look at October activity and price pressures. Watch the prices-paid parts for oil pass-through.

week.name: UMich Sentiment, final (Oct)
week.why: Inflation expectations matter here. Rising expectations would make the Fed's job harder the week before its meeting.

stocks.title: S&P 500 near a record while 200-plus members sit 30% off highs
stocks.detail: Traders are calling it a bear-bull paradox: a handful of AI mega caps carry the index while most stocks lag. Bulls see bargains if oil eases, bears see a fragile, narrow market.

stocks.title: TSMC says AI demand is extremely strong, but chips keep sliding
stocks.detail: TSMC posted a record quarter with revenue up 41% and guided Q4 higher, yet US chip names are red again today. The disconnect is the big debate for NVDA, MRVL and INTC holders.

stocks.title: MSCI rules could boot Strategy from global indexes
stocks.detail: New MSCI rules treat firms dominated by bitcoin holdings as non-operating. Strategy and Metaplanet top the possible deletion list after Nov 30, which could force passive selling.

stocks.title: Indonesia stocks crash 11% on an MSCI downgrade threat
stocks.detail: MSCI opened a consultation on moving Indonesia out of emerging market status over ownership transparency worries. It was the worst one-day drop since 1998 and trading was halted.

tech.title: Tesla's new Roadster reveal sparks a design fight with Porsche
tech.detail: Tesla showed the next Roadster Thursday night with compressed-air thrusters and a 2028 target, the same day Porsche unveiled its Mission S concept. Heritage versus spectacle is the debate.

tech.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arrive with Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU
tech.detail: ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI are shipping them with up to 128GB of unified memory for running AI models locally. Early tests put them near NVIDIA's DGX Spark desktop.

tech.title: Sam Altman says AI disruption is slower than he expected
tech.detail: Altman said habits and company inertia have slowed AI's impact since GPT-4, and called that a good thing. Big Tech keeps borrowing heavily to fund AI buildouts anyway.

tech.title: Bluesky users push back on its new Attie AI builder
tech.detail: Attie lets anyone make social sites, games and quizzes from prompts. Many longtime users say it betrays the platform's non-AI roots.

world.title: Iran strikes another tanker and vows to push US ships farther out
world.detail: Iran released video of a burning tanker east of Hormuz and says US warships are already 500 km from its coast. Two dozen-plus incidents in weeks keep oil flows and prices tense.

world.title: World Food Day: 645 million people went hungry last year
world.detail: The UN theme is Innovate today, nourish tomorrow. Leaders are pushing tech and local food systems while people flood X with their favorite dishes.

world.title: BBC News launches on YouTube, stirring UK licence fee fears
world.detail: The live channel targets younger viewers in the UK and US. Many Brits worry it is a step toward charging the TV licence fee for streaming platforms.

world.title: UN committee passes a Russian-backed resolution on modern colonialism
world.detail: The vote was 85-49 with 23 abstentions. The US, UK and EU voted no, citing Russia's invasion of Ukraine as a contradiction.

fact.claim: October is historically the S&P 500's worst month on average.
fact.explain: October has the scary reputation because of the 1929 and 1987 crashes, but its average return is positive. September is the month that has been weakest on average over the long run.

word.definition: Mental calm and steadiness, especially when things are stressful or going against you.
word.example: After a rough week, he met the premarket bounce with equanimity and stuck to his plan.

gbot.name: GROK
gbot.say: TSLA's 3% gap got cut to 1%, but it's still green while QQQ bleeds. 363 is the line to hold into the opex close.

items.title: TSLA levels for the rest of opex day
items.detail: Today's range so far is 363.37 to 370.58, and Thursday closed at 362.44. Holding above 363 keeps the bounce alive going into Wednesday's earnings after the close.

items.title: Your portfolio is beating the tape today
items.detail: You're up about 1% while QQQ is down 1%, because the TSLA stack is carrying you. QLD is the drag, and it moves double QQQ, so chip weakness hits it hardest.

items.title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III is a problem
items.detail: He's averaging a league-best 6.2 yards per carry through four games in KC. The 0-5 Chargers come to Arrowhead Sunday with Justin Herbert under fire.

items.title: Cool tech: NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops
items.detail: Arm-based Grace CPU plus a Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of unified memory, built to run big AI models right on a laptop. A real shot at Apple's M-series and Intel.

sports.title: Chiefs host the 0-5 Chargers Sunday at Arrowhead
sports.detail: Rashee Rice's hamstring is the question after he sat Thursday, and Josh Simmons was limited. Andy Reid's Friday update is the one to watch before locking anything in.

sports.title: Kenneth Walker III leads the NFL at 6.2 yards per carry
sports.detail: Seattle fans are lamenting letting him walk after their Super Bowl win. The Chargers' run defense gets the next look on Sunday.

sports.title: AFC West: Broncos win 17-14 in OT, move to 4-2
sports.detail: Denver's defense carried them past Seattle Thursday night while Bo Nix threw for just 107 yards.

sports.title: Lakers roster crunch hits Oct 19
sports.detail: LA has to get to 15 players. Reports say talks to send Dalton Knecht to the Bucks for Jericho Sims look unlikely, so a waiver is still on the table.
